propositions.text: The claimant is a 34-year-old West Bank resident with a Palestinian Authority passport claiming refugee protection under sections 96 and 97(1) of the Act.
propositions.quote: XXX XXXX XXXXXX, (the "claimant" or the "XXXX"), is a 34 year-old resident of the West Bank holding a passport issued by the Palestinian Authority and is claiming refugee protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration Refugee Protection Act (the "Act").1

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is a 34-year-old West Bank resident with a Palestinian Authority passport claiming refugee protection under the Act, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant's allegations are contained in his Personal Information Form narrative.
propositions.quote: The claimant's allegations are found in his Personal Information Form (PIF) narrative.2

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's allegations are found in his Personal Information Form narrative, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant is from Palestine and served in the military in Ramallah with certain duties related to prisoners.
propositions.quote: The claimant comes from XXXX, Palestine. He is XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX XXXXX Military Service in Ramallah. His duties included XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX. In the case of the prisoners, XXXXXXXXXXXXXX XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is from Palestine and served in the military in Ramallah with duties related to prisoners, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant received two phone demands to assist anti-PA elements and notified his PA military supervisor after each call.
propositions.quote: The XXXX received two telephone demands to assist anti-PA elements, such as Hamas or the Al-jihad Al-islami movement by finding that XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX XXXX. He notified his supervisor, a XXXXXXXXX in the PA military, after each call.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant received two phone demands to assist anti-PA elements and notified his PA military supervisor after each call, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant felt the second call was more serious, mentioning Hamas and a death in intelligence prison, and notified his supervisor who told him to be cautious.
propositions.quote: The claimant felt the second call to be the more serious as the caller mentioned Hamas and the death of someone in the intelligence prison. The caller blamed the XXXX, although he cannot recall the name or circumstance, and felt the claim "absurd". Again, he notified his supervisor, in a panic, but was told merely to be cautious, which did not assist the claimant in knowing what to do.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant felt the second call was more serious, mentioning Hamas and a death, and his supervisor told him to be cautious, court states.

propositions.text: A month after the second call, the claimant's home was shot at and he received a threatening call from an unidentified Hamas representative; he notified his supervisor who did nothing, so he left Palestine for Canada.
propositions.quote: A month after the second call, his home was shot up by unknown attackers. The next day he "...received a call from the same unidentified Hamas representative..." that, although he had survived, the next time the bullet would surely hit him. He notified his supervisor who did nothing, so he left Palestine for Canada on XXXX 2008.

paragraphs.summary: A month after the second call, the claimant's home was shot at and he received a threatening call; his supervisor did nothing, so he left Palestine, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant made his refugee protection claim in Canada on 1 August 2008, just over one month after leaving Palestine.
propositions.quote: The claimant made his claim for protection in Canada on 1 August 2008, just over one month later.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant made his refugee protection claim in Canada on 1 August 2008, court states.

propositions.text: The panel determined the claimant is not a Convention refugee as he lacks a well-founded fear of persecution based on a Convention ground.
propositions.quote: The panel has determined that the claimant is not a Convention refugee in that he does not have a well-founded fear of persecution in Palestine based on a Convention ground.

propositions.text: The panel also determined the claimant is not a person in need of protection as removal to Palestine does not pose a danger of torture or risk to life or cruel treatment.
propositions.quote: The panel also determines that the claimant is not a person in need of protection as there are no substantial grounds to believe that the claimant's removal to Palestine will subject him to a danger of torture and, on a balance of probabilities, he does not face a risk to his life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.

paragraphs.summary: The panel determined the claimant is not a Convention refugee and not in need of protection as removal to Palestine poses no substantial risk, court states.

propositions.text: The determinative issues in this claim are credibility and state protection.
propositions.quote: The determinative issues in this claim are credibility and state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The determinative issues are credibility and state protection, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant's identity as a Palestinian national and military worker is established by testimony and documents including his PA passport.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity as a national of Palestine has been established by his testimony and the claimant's documents, including his passport from the Palestinian Authority (PA).3 Also, the claimant's identity, XXXXXXXXXXX who worked for the military, was established4 by the claimant's testimony and the materials disclosed.5

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's identity as a Palestinian national and military worker is established by testimony and documents, court finds.

propositions.text: To be a Convention refugee, fear of persecution must be based on one of the five grounds in the Convention refugee definition.
propositions.quote: For the claimant to be a Convention refugee, his fear of persecution must be by reason of one of the five grounds enumerated in the Convention refugee definition.

propositions.text: Counsel suggested the claim be considered under imputed political opinion.
propositions.quote: Counsel suggested that this claim be considered under imputed political opinion.

propositions.text: The claimant's fear of persecution is linked to one of the five grounds, as submitted.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant's fear of persecution is linked to one of the five grounds, as submitted.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's fear must be based on a Convention ground; counsel suggested imputed political opinion; court finds fear linked to a ground.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges he would be killed by Hamas or anti-PA allies for non-compliance regarding political prisoners, which would be persecution if well-founded.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleged that, should he return to Palestine, he would be killed by Hamas or its anti-PA allies for not complying with their requirements regarding political prisoners. Such harm would amount to persecution for a Convention ground if his claim were well-founded.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges risk of killing by Hamas or anti-PA allies for non-compliance, which would be persecution if well-founded, court finds.

propositions.text: The claimant submitted a psychiatric assessment diagnosing anxiety and depression, but it cannot substitute for the panel's credibility assessment.
propositions.quote: The claimant submitted a psychiatric assessment which is discussed more at length below. I mention it here as the diagnosis of the doctor in Canada cannot substitute for the panel's credibility assessment of the claimant.

propositions.text: The panel tried to question the claimant sensitively given the diagnosis and noted counsel's mention of claimant's weight loss and PTSD-related recall or concentration problems.
propositions.quote: However, the doctor notes that the claimant suffers from anxiety and depression. The panel attempted to question the claimant with sensitivity to this diagnosis. Furthermore, counsel brought to my attention the clear weight loss suffered by the claimant6 and noted that persons suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder often have recall problems or problems in concentration.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant submitted a psychiatric assessment diagnosing anxiety and depression; the panel questioned sensitively and noted counsel's observations, court states.

propositions.text: The panel did not observe any problems with the claimant's recall or concentration despite the PTSD diagnosis of moderate symptoms.
propositions.quote: The panel did not notice the claimant had any particular problem with his ability to recall or describe events he alleged occurred. The panel did not notice any problems that could be ascribed to a problem of concentration. I note that the psychiatric assessment diagnoses moderate symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder.

paragraphs.summary: The panel did not observe recall or concentration problems despite PTSD diagnosis, court finds.

propositions.text: The claimant's testimony about fear of anti-PA militants is not credible mainly because he was employed by the PA military when problems arose.
propositions.quote: I found the claimant's testimony not to be credible with respect to his fear of anti-PA militants for several reasons, mainly because the claimant was employed by the government of Palestine and worked within the military when the alleged problems arose.

propositions.text: The claimant did not avail himself of state protection as required, intertwined with the credibility finding.
propositions.quote: Intertwined with this finding, I find that the claimant did not avail himself of his state's protection as he is required to do.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's testimony is not credible because he was employed by the PA military and did not seek state protection, court finds.

propositions.text: The panel examined the claimant's allegations of threats from Hamas in Palestine in 2008, including two threatening phone calls.
propositions.quote: The panel first looked at the threats from the Hamas in Palestine that the claimant alleges. The claimant testified he was subjected to threatening phone calls from Hamas on two occasions in 2008.

propositions.text: The claimant wrote in his PIF that callers demanded cooperation with Hamas.
propositions.quote: He wrote in his Personal Information Form (PIF) narrative that the callers demanded he cooperate XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The panel examined the claimant's allegations of two threatening phone calls from Hamas demanding cooperation, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant testified the second call blamed him for a colleague's death in intelligence prison and his residence was shot at about a month later.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that, after the second threatening call, the caller told him that he had failed them to the point that one of their colleagues had died in intelligence prison because he had XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, and that Hamas blamed him for this death. Subsequently, about one month after the death threat, someone shot up his residence and fled the scene by car.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified the second call blamed him for a colleague's death and his residence was shot at a month later, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant said he reported threats to two superiors, but their response was not credible or cogent.
propositions.quote: The claimant wrote in his PIF narrative that he went to his "supervisor" each time. In his testimony, the claimant stated he had two superiors, a Captain and a Colonel.7 This is the core of the claim but the description of the officers' response to his concerns is neither cogent or credible.

propositions.text: The claimant did not disclose his military rank in his PIF but disclosed it to CIC in his Background Information form.
propositions.quote: Although the claimant never disclosed his military rank in his PIF,8 the claimant disclosed to the Minister of Citizenship and Immigration (CIC) in his Background Information form9 filed with his refugee claim, that the claimant set out that he was, from XXXX 2005 to XXXX 2008, a XXXX XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, as well as working for the PA XXXXXXXXXXX XXXX during the same period.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant reported threats to two superiors but their response was not credible; he disclosed military rank to CIC but not in PIF, court states.

propositions.text: The Board's documentary evidence describes the West Bank's division into Areas A, B, and C with varying PA and Israeli control.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence provided by the Board is found in the national documentation package for Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT) dated 29 November 2010. The OPT is formed of the West Bank (including East Jerusalem) and the Gaza Strip. The Israeli-Palestinian Interim Agreement on the West Bank and the Gaza Strip concluded in September 1995 divided the West Bank into three zones: Area A consisting of approximately 17.2% of the West Bank was under sole Palestinian jurisdiction and security control, although Israel retained authority over access to and from the zone; about 23.8% (Area B) was under Israeli military control, with the PA responsible for civil administration and public order; the remaining 59% (Area C) remained under Israeli military occupation. The total area of the territory over which the PA will eventually assume control, and the extent of its jurisdiction there, remain subject to 'final status' talks. The population of the West Bank is approximately 2.35 million. The vast majority of Palestinians in the OPT are Muslim. Gaza City is the administration centre for the PA and Ramallah is the PA's administrative centre in the West Bank. The status of Jerusalem remains subject to negotiation on so-called 'final status' issues under the Oslo accords.10

paragraphs.summary: The Board's evidence describes the West Bank's division into Areas A, B, and C with varying PA and Israeli control, court states.

propositions.text: The UK and US reports describe the PA's establishment, governance, and Hamas's control in Gaza and West Bank.
propositions.quote: According to the UK Report,11 the Palestinian Liberation Organization and Israel established the Palestinian Authority (PA) in 1994. The PA is intended to serve as the governing body of the West Bank and Gaza until a final agreement is reached in the peace process. According to the US Department of State in its introduction to the OPT,12 The Palestinian Authority (PA) has a democratically elected president and legislative council. The president appoints the prime minister who forms a cabinet in consultation with the president; the PA exercised varying degrees of authority over the Palestinian population in the West Bank because of the Israel Defense Force's (IDF) continuing presence, little authority in Gaza, and none over Israeli residents of the West Bank or Arab residents of East Jerusalem. In 2005 Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) Chairman Mahmoud Abbas won 62 percent of the vote in a presidential election regarded as generally free and fair. In 2006 Palestinian Legislative Council (PLC) elections, Hamas, a terrorist organization, backed candidates under the "Reform and Change Movement" ticket and won 74 of 132 seats in elections that generally met democratic standards. In March 2007 Hamas formed a national unity government (NUG) with the Fatah party, but after three months Hamas staged a violent takeover of PA government installations in Gaza and killed hundreds in the Fatah movement and PA security forces. President Abbas then dismissed the NUG and appointed a cabinet of independents led by Prime Minister Salam Fayyad that has governed the West Bank, while elements of the former Hamas government formed the ruling authority in Gaza where it selectively applied the laws and legal structures of the PA. President Abbas and his subordinates controlled PA security forces in the West Bank. Armed militias and terrorist organizations were still active in some areas. In Gaza, Hamas controlled security forces. Other armed factions and terrorist organizations were active in Gaza. The Israeli government maintained effective control of its security forces.

paragraphs.summary: UK and US reports describe the PA's establishment, governance, Hamas's control in Gaza, and ongoing armed factions, court states.

propositions.text: The Economist's backgrounder describes Palestine's political system as vibrant but violent, with a split between Hamas in Gaza and Fatah in the West Bank.
propositions.quote: Although it lacks many of a sovereign state's common features, Palestine's political system is vibrant and pluralistic, though violent at times. Until June 2007, parts of the West Bank and all of the Gaza Strip... Hamas has a grip on Gaza, while Fatah retains control in the West Bank.

paragraphs.summary: The Economist's backgrounder describes Palestine's political system as vibrant but violent, split between Hamas in Gaza and Fatah in the West Bank.

propositions.text: Jane's Sentinel Country assessment notes the Palestinian Territories are divided into Abbas-led West Bank and Hamas-led Gaza, with failed unity talks.
propositions.quote: The Palestinian Territories are effectively divided into two political units: an internationally recognised and accepted Abbas-led West Bank under tight Israeli security control, and a Hamas-led internationally isolated Gaza Strip... Attempts are underway to bring the two factions together... but talks ended without agreement.

paragraphs.summary: Jane's assessment notes the Palestinian Territories are divided into Abbas-led West Bank and Hamas-led Gaza, with failed unity talks.

propositions.text: The panel infers the claimant is not credible due to inconsistency about fearing Islamists versus another group.
propositions.quote: The panel takes a negative credibility inference that the claimant, a Sunni Muslim, wrote in his IMM5474 that he feared being killed by Islamists and not the group he stated in his testimony and in his PIF narrative that he feared.

propositions.text: Inconsistency between Port of Entry notes and PIF narrative is a way to determine claimant credibility.
propositions.quote: The court has stated that inconsistency between Port of Entry notes and the PIF narrative is one way to determine if a claimant is credible, as the first story is often the most credible story.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant not credible due to inconsistency about feared persecutors, citing inconsistency between Port of Entry notes and PIF narrative as a credibility test.

propositions.text: The claimant's story is not corroborated by documentary evidence or evidence from former commanding officers.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant's story is not corroborated by the documentary evidence and the claimant has not provided any evidence from his former commanding officer or officers to corroborate his claim.

propositions.text: The claimant failed to provide military discharge papers or other evidence to assist credibility.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the claimant failed to provide a copy of his military discharge papers or anything else that might assist the panel to find the claim credible.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's story lacks corroboration from documents or commanding officers and he failed to provide military discharge papers.

propositions.text: Claimant must provide evidence of being asked to comply with improper directions by terrorists, which he failed to do.
propositions.quote: If the claimant has been asked to comply with improper directions by terrorists... he is obliged to provide some evidence that this happened... which he failed to do.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant failed to provide evidence of being asked to comply with improper directions by terrorists as required.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to take steps like filing complaints or seeking protection from PA or Israeli authorities before fleeing.
propositions.quote: He could have filed a complaint. He could have spoken to the PA and its representatives. He could have spoken to the Israeli security authorities... many things the claimant could have done short of fleeing Palestine for Canada.

propositions.text: The claimant is not credible and failed to avail himself of Palestinian Authority protection.
propositions.quote: Accordingly, I find that the claimant is not credible and that the claimant failed to avail himself of the protection of the Palestinian Authority.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is not credible and failed to seek protection from the Palestinian Authority or others before fleeing.

propositions.text: Counsel did not distinguish the situation in Gaza from that in the West Bank regarding Hamas.
propositions.quote: In regards to the Counsel's submissions regarding Hamas, I note that he has not distinguished the situation in Gaza from that in the West Bank.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel failed to distinguish the situation in Gaza from the West Bank regarding Hamas.

propositions.text: The claimant is not a Convention refugee as no evidence shows it was unreasonable to seek state protection.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the claimant is not a Convention refugee as there is no evidence it would have been unreasonable for the claimant to obtain the protection of his state...

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is not a Convention refugee due to lack of evidence that state protection was unreasonable to seek.

propositions.text: The claimant provided a psychiatric report from Dr. XXXXXXX, a qualified medical doctor and psychiatrist.
propositions.quote: The claimant provided a report dated XXXX 2010 from Dr. XXXXXXXXX, a medical doctor and psychiatrist retained by counsel to provide an assessment for the hearing.

propositions.text: Dr. XXXXXXX has extensive psychiatric credentials and private practice experience.
propositions.quote: Dr. XXXXXXX is currently the XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX (ON) XXXXXXXXXXXX... and is currently in private practice having been XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX from 19XX to 19XX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant submitted a psychiatric report from Dr. XXXXXXX, a qualified psychiatrist with extensive credentials and experience.

propositions.text: Dr. XXXXXXX's assessment recounts claimant's history and notes panic attacks starting about a year ago, with ongoing symptoms.
propositions.quote: The author recounts... the claimant suffered a panic attack "about a year ago"... Since that time... the claimant has been treated with medication and has improved somewhat but is still: "getting similar attacks almost daily..."

paragraphs.summary: Dr. XXXXXXX's assessment notes claimant's panic attacks starting about a year ago and ongoing symptoms despite treatment.

propositions.text: No previous or family psychiatric history; claimant's cognitive difficulties seem improved.
propositions.quote: There is no previous or family psychiatric history... Although the claimant reported having some cognitive difficulties... this "...seems to have improved."

paragraphs.summary: The claimant has no prior psychiatric history and reported cognitive difficulties appear improved.

propositions.text: Dr. XXXXXXX saw claimant once and diagnosed PTSD, reflux esophagitis, and stress from trauma, with GAF 60.
propositions.quote: Dr. XXXXXXX appears to have seen the claimant only once... His "...diagnosis according to DSM4TR is..." Axis I: post-traumatic stress disorder; Axis III: reflux esophagitis; Axis IV: stress from traumatizing events... Axis V: GAF 60.

paragraphs.summary: Dr. XXXXXXX diagnosed claimant with PTSD, reflux esophagitis, and stress from trauma, with a GAF score of 60 after one assessment.

propositions.text: Claimant takes Prevacid for reflux and Lorazepam, but psychiatrist did not explain Lorazepam use.
propositions.quote: The claimant is taking Prevacid 30mg... and Lorazepam 0.5mg daily... he does not explain the prescription for Lorazepam or the indications for its use here.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant takes Prevacid and Lorazepam, but the psychiatrist did not explain the Lorazepam prescription.

propositions.text: Counsel disclosed articles explaining DSM-IV and its axes, describing mental disorder classifications and GAF scale.
propositions.quote: Counsel's article indicates that the DSM-IV stands for... 'bible' of psychiatric diagnosis... Axis I identifies mental disorders; Axis II identifies personality disorders... Axis IV is used... to assess... Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF).

paragraphs.summary: Counsel disclosed articles explaining DSM-IV and the GAF scale for psychiatric diagnosis.

propositions.text: Dr. XXXXXXX did not explain how he arrived at his diagnosis or what tests he used.
propositions.quote: Dr. XXXXXXX does not provide information as to how he arrived at his diagnosis or what tests, if any, he conducted to assist him in his evaluation and assessment.

propositions.text: Counsel's notes in the report are unclear if they reflect doctor's findings or editorial notes.
propositions.quote: Counsel has flagged various entries... with the word "NOTE" and an arrow... no indication if that is a finding of the doctor or an editorial note by counsel.

paragraphs.summary: Dr. XXXXXXX did not explain his diagnostic methods and counsel's notes in the report are unclear if they reflect doctor's findings or editorial comments.

propositions.text: Psychiatrist concludes claimant's symptoms are consistent with reported threats and believes PTSD will remit if claimant stays in Canada.
propositions.quote: The symptoms described by XXXXXXXX are consistent with the experiences of threats... I believe his post-traumatic stress disorder will remit if he is allowed to stay in this country...

paragraphs.summary: The psychiatrist concludes claimant's symptoms align with reported threats and PTSD may remit if claimant remains in Canada.

propositions.text: It appears Dr. XXXXXXX concludes claimant has PTSD with moderate symptoms, but this is unclear from the report separation.
propositions.quote: it appears... that Dr. XXXXXXX concludes that the claimant suffers from post-traumatic stress disorder with "moderate symptoms".

paragraphs.summary: It appears Dr. XXXXXXX concludes claimant has PTSD with moderate symptoms, but this is unclear from the report.

propositions.text: An article on PTSD in refugees notes refugees face traumatic events including forced isolation and ongoing stressors in exile and resettlement.
propositions.quote: Prior to flight, individuals who become refugees may face a wide variety of traumatic events... the most commonly reported traumatic event was forced isolation... Additional chronic stressors... include socioeconomic disadvantages, poor physical health, and the collapse of social support.

paragraphs.summary: An article notes refugees face traumatic events like forced isolation and ongoing stressors during exile and resettlement.

propositions.text: The panel is not qualified to dispute the psychiatrist's conclusion but cannot conclude claimant's depression results from reported events in Palestine.
propositions.quote: The panel member does not possess a doctorate in medicine... but the panel cannot conclude that the claimant's depression is a result of what the claimant reported happened to him in Palestine.

paragraphs.summary: The panel cannot dispute the psychiatrist but cannot conclude claimant's depression results from events in Palestine.

propositions.text: Claimant's depression and anxiety may result from many factors including isolation and hostility in Canada, not just past trauma.
propositions.quote: There could be many reasons why the claimant may be depressed and anxious, including... isolation and hostility in Canada... socio-economic disadvantages... without social or emotional support...

propositions.text: The panel gives little weight to the psychiatric assessment to establish claimant's subjective well-founded fear of persecution.
propositions.quote: Keeping these other possible factors... the panel can give little weight to the assessment of Dr. XXXXXXX as a basis for determining that the claimant's stated fears are objectively credible...

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's depression may stem from many factors and gives little weight to the psychiatric assessment for fear credibility.

propositions.text: The panel gives little weight to Dr. XXXXXXX's report and conclusions.
propositions.quote: The panel can give this report and Dr. XXXXXXX conclusions little weight.

propositions.text: Dr. XXXXXXX's report is based primarily on what the claimant told him.
propositions.quote: The panel notes that Dr. XXXXXXX report is based primarily on what the claimant told him.

propositions.text: The panel does not believe the claimant and does not find him credible.
propositions.quote: Given that the panel does not believe the claimant and does not find him credible,

propositions.text: The panel finds the psychiatrist's conclusion about symptoms consistent with threats and attempt on life not determinative.
propositions.quote: the panel finds that the conclusion of the psychiatrist, "The symptoms described by XXXXXXXXX are consistent with the experiences of threats and the attempt on his life he reported to me" are not determinative,

propositions.text: A psychiatric report cannot serve as a cure-all for deficiencies in a claimant's testimony.
propositions.quote: "...such a report cannot possibly serve as a cure-all for any and all deficiencies in a claimant's testimony"26.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds Dr. XXXXXXX's report unreliable because it relies on the claimant's testimony, which the panel does not find credible, and thus the psychiatrist's conclusions are not determinative.

propositions.text: The panel found the claimant is not a Convention refugee.
propositions.quote: Having found that the claimant is not a Convention refugee,

propositions.text: Whether the harm feared by the claimant amounts to risk of life or cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.
propositions.quote: the panel then considered whether the harm allegedly feared by the claimant would amount to a risk of life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.

propositions.text: There is no evidence on a balance of probabilities that the claimant faces such risk.
propositions.quote: There is no evidence before the Board, on a balance of probabilities, that the claimant faces such risk.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the claimant is not a Convention refugee and sees no evidence that he faces risk of life or cruel treatment.

propositions.text: The claimant's family still lives in XXXXXX.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the claimant's family still lives in XXXXXX

propositions.text: There is no evidence of anything happening to the claimant's family.
propositions.quote: and there is no evidence of anything happening to them.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes the claimant's family still lives in XXXXXX with no evidence of harm to them.

propositions.text: The panel does not find the claimant's allegations that there is no serious possibility of persecution from Hamas or Islamist groups.
propositions.quote: the panel does not find the claimant's allegations that there is no serious possibility that he would face persecution from the Hamas or other Islamist groups.

propositions.text: On a balance of probabilities, the claimant does not face risk to life, cruel treatment, or torture if returned to Palestine.
propositions.quote: The panel also finds that, on a balance of probabilities, the claimant does not face a risk to life or risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, or a danger of torture if he were to return to Palestine,

propositions.text: Reasons analyzed above under section 96 of the Act support this finding.
propositions.quote: for the reasons analyzed above under section 96 of the Act.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no serious possibility of persecution or risk of harm to the claimant if returned to Palestine, based on prior analysis.

propositions.text: The panel determines the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection and rejects his claim.
propositions.quote: the panel determines that XXXXXXXXXX is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection and therefore rejects his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes the claimant is not a Convention refugee or protected person and rejects the claim.
